title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.starting_material: Equimolar or near‐equimolar mixtures of refractory transition metals (e.g., Mo, Nb, Ta, W, V) – guessed
recollection.intervention: CALPHAD‐guided composition screening followed by arc‐melting and homogenization anneal – guessed
recollection.structure: Single‐phase body‐centered cubic (BCC) high‐entropy alloy solid solution – guessed
recollection.mechanism: High‐entropy mixing and lattice‐distortion effects stabilizing the BCC phase and suppressing ordered/secondary phases at high temperature – guessed
recollection.results: Demonstrated a single‐phase BCC alloy with >1000 MPa yield strength at room temperature and retention of >800 MPa at 1000 °C, hardness ≈500 HV – guessed

score.note: The intervention is misidentified as CALPHAD screening and adds a homogenization anneal; the actual strategy screened 38,326 compositions using modulus, VEC, and density calculations before arc melting. The single-phase BCC structure is correctly recalled. The proposed mechanism is wrong: the paper emphasizes reduced VEC, a lower Peierls–Nabarro barrier, enhanced dislocation slip, delayed cracking, and work hardening—not entropy-driven phase stabilization. The room-temperature yield-strength estimate is close to the actual 1115 MPa, but the high-temperature result is unsupported, the hardness is only approximate, and the key 35.7% fracture strain and 2550 MPa compressive strength are omitted.
